title: Cumulative Sum That Resets on Partition Change
description: Compute a **running total of sales that automatically resets** at the start of each quota period for each salesperson. Use SUM() OVER with a composite PARTITION BY (salesperson_id, quota_period) to achieve the reset behavior.
solution_sql: SELECT salesperson_id, quota_period, sale_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY salesperson_id, quota_period ORDER BY sale_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total FROM sales ORDER BY salesperson_id, quota_period, sale_date
hints: PARTITION BY (salesperson_id, quota_period) creates a separate window for each salesperson-quarter combination — the running total naturally resets when the partition changes.
ORDER BY sale_date with ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ensures the running total accumulates chronologically within each partition.
explanation: The composite partition key (salesperson_id, quota_period) means each unique combination gets its own window. When salesperson 1 transitions from Q1-2026 to Q2-2026, the window resets — the running total starts fresh at 800 for the first Q2 sale. S1 Q1: 500→1200→1800. S1 Q2: 800→1200. S2 Q1: 300→800→1250. S2 Q2: 600→1300. This pattern is used in quota tracking, budget period resets, and cumulative KPIs.
